note: Each subsystem is scored on the metric its task implies. No single accuracy figure exists across forecasting, screening, survival and event detection.

rows.why_not_95: a model fitted ON the test fold -- which has seen the answers -- still only reaches WAPE 0.0547, so WAPE 0.05 is below the information floor of this data

rows.task: route each batch GOOD / RISK / REJECT
rows.headline_metric: unsafe recall at a capped false-accept rate
rows.why_not_naive_accuracy: naive 2-class accuracy is ~0.87 against a 0.84 majority-class baseline, so it would flatter a model that reviews nothing

rows.task: remaining safe hours as an interval + hard lower bound
rows.headline_metric: share above the conservative lower bound
rows.why_this_metric: a point forecast has no accuracy; the operational question is how often the hard lower bound is safe, which is the 0.95-capped number

rows.task: detect faults across compressor and door cycles
rows.headline_metric: episode recall (an incident is found at all)
rows.why_not_row_accuracy: rows inside a fault are not independent observations; missing one of 200 readings in an incident is not 1/200 of the outcome, which is why this is scored per incident

rows.task: assign collection stops under vehicle, capacity and time limits
rows.headline_metric: mean stop coverage (share of stops served)

secondary.scoring_note: on-time PORTIONS delivered before the food deadline, not stops visited

rows.why_this_metric: this is a solver, not a classifier: there is no correct answer to compare against, only coverage delivered and food waste avoided
